"description": "

The files here represent the minimal dataset underlying the study findings reported in the article Spatiotemporal Modelling of Bacterial Meningitis Outbreaks using Climatic Drivers in Africa. This includes the values behind the means, standard deviations and other measures reported, as well as the values used to build graphs.

The files are organised into folders as follows:

Folder 1 represents the underlying data for Figures 1a and 1b: respectively, the district-ADM1 level map of outbreak events (map_data.csv) and the line graph of district-months affected by an outbreak within our study period (2003\u20132022) (outbreaks_over_time.csv).

The file anonymised_outbreak_climate_data.csv is the anonymised version of the final climate dataset, with the same structure and variables as the original analysis data. Outbreaks here are coded as 1/0, indicating whether or not a district experienced a meningitis outbreak within a given month.

Folder 2 shows the WAIC and DIC results of our examination and selection of spatial and temporal random-effects structures for the climatic INLA model. Temporal structures (AR1, RW1 and RW2) were compared, considering month as both a continuous and cyclic variable (model_comparison_temporal.csv), alongside four spatial structures (Besag, Besag proper, BYM and BYM2) (model_comparison_spatial.csv).

Folder 3 contains the results of our univariate and multivariate stepwise linear model-building process. Here, each file provides the WAIC and DIC values for all variables at each step. Temperature, zonal wind, dust and humidity were added to the model, initially as linear variables in each sequential step.

Folder 4 contains the results (WAIC and DIC) of our evaluation of non-linear relationships using RW2 effects, carried out in a stepwise fashion. This led to the inclusion of an RW2 effect for temperature (rw2_test_results_step1.csv), but in the second step of the analysis, the inclusion of any additional RW2 effects did not improve model fit (rw2_test_results_step2.csv). Following this, we carried out an additional examination of potential interactions between zonal wind and dust through the creation of additional zonal wind strength and direction variables.

The text file final_model_summary.csv provides the INLA model summary of the final model used within cross-validation and for determining climatic variable associations with outbreak occurrence.

Folder 5 contains the results of the Brier score, log loss, recall and the ROC curve (Figure 5 within the paper), stratified across each fold within our k-fold cross-validation process.

Folder 6 contains the underlying data for Figures 2\u20134, which show the log odds of outbreak occurrence within a given range of temperature, with the variable converted back to degrees Celsius (Figure 2b \u2013 temp_non_lin_effect_fixed.csv). Alongside this, we have also generated a histogram showing the distribution of district-months affected by outbreaks across a range of temperatures (Figure 2a \u2013 histo_data.csv).

Following on from this, we have extracted and generated plots for the dust and directional zonal wind interaction (Figure 3 \u2013 aod_by_winddir_logodds_data.csv), the RW2 temporal effect (Figure 4 \u2013 temporal_effect.csv) and the BYM2 spatial effect (SI \u2013 spatial_bym2_mean_data.csv).
